locator.text: Equation (5.46), p. 61, in the proof of Proposition 5.5

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The quantity bounded is the same object — slowStage is literally χ(a_j q)·q^{2hj}·f_j (coefficientWeight spells the weight out) — with the same prefactor 2^{-j} and the same exponent q^{jh}, i.e. half of the 2jh weight is spent and half survives, exactly as in (5.46). Differences in encoding: (i) the paper's family 𝒟 = {q∂_q, ∂_X, ∂_η} with multi-index I is replaced by the full m-th Fréchet jet of the blown-up map F ∘ scaleMap q, which realises q∂_q in the q slot and plain ∂ in the inner slots; the rewriting between |𝒟^I| with |I| = m and ‖blownJet m‖ is the usual equivalence of a norm on the m-linear jet with the max over the m directional derivatives, up to the Stirling combinations relating (q∂_q)^k and q^k∂_q^k, and is bounded both ways by dimensional constants. (ii) Lean's index range 1 ≤ j, m ≤ j + 2 contains the paper's n ≥ max{2,|I|}: for m ≤ j + 2 Lean asks for more (also the two jets above the paper's threshold) and the paper's constraint n ≥ 2 is not imposed because the j = 0 stage is defined to be 0. (iii) Lean restricts to 0 < q ≤ 1 and w in a compact inner set K, where the paper states it for the stage on its support. (iv) The generic companion CutStageBounds, used by the diagonal machinery, keeps a loss q^{-L m} in the exponent (L = CutStageEstimates.cutLoss) and so is weaker than (5.46); it is the blown form in AdmissibleScales that reproduces (5.46) without loss.
